summary: This revision extends the Files explorer already in the app instead of adding a second file system path: a new plain-Rust ops module sits beside the existing one-level lister, five thin Tauri commands sit behind typed wrappers in src/api/explorer.ts, and the existing ExplorerPanel/useExplorer gain selection, inline create/rename, a Move action through the existing folder picker, drag-and-drop onto folder rows, and one Recycle-Bin delete confirmation built from the shared Dialog. Rename and move update the open editor entries inside the same command (Store::repoint, Store::close_under); the window then re-lists open editors (useEditor.resync) so tab paths, titles and derived tab groups follow, and delete removes the affected tabs. The terminal model gains one boolean that is true when missing: Rust gets serde default plus a manual Default, TypeScript treats undefined as true, EditPane shows a labelled switch, and start_all/stop_all, engine up/readiness, the Start/Stop button and every app status dot are computed from executable terminals only; F5 already runs that same token, so this revision adds only the F5 key hint and keeps refresh on its buttons and palette entry (R12). The command palette gets a mobile-first base with a desktop media query (R10). At a hundred times the data the work stays bounded: one directory level per request (existing 1000-row/10k-scan caps), one OS call per file operation, tab updates scan only open tabs, and post-operation refresh touches only the affected folder levels plus expanded folders in the existing 100-level LRU cache. No polling, listeners, network calls or full-tree walks are added; the new costs are one small Recycle-Bin crate, five command registrations and one boolean per terminal. The five commands are explorer_create_file(parent, name) and explorer_create_folder(parent, name), each returning the new path; explorer_rename(path, newName) returning the new path; explorer_move(path, destDir) returning the new path; and explorer_delete(path) returning nothing. All are async, run on a blocking worker, and their results are typed in src/api/explorer.ts. No new capability permission is needed: custom commands stay under core:default plus dialog:allow-open, which the Move folder picker already uses, and the content security policy does not change.

additions.title: Send explorer deletes to the Recycle Bin with the trash crate
additions.why: Deleting from the explorer must stay recoverable instead of removing a person's files for good.
acceptance: The Windows Rust dependencies declare the small, maintained trash crate in src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
Deleting a file or folder through the explorer places it in the Recycle Bin.
When the Recycle Bin refuses an item, the command returns a readable refusal and leaves the item on disk.
No code path falls back to a permanent delete.

additions.title: Bump the app version in all three files
additions.why: The project ships one version number and every feature release keeps the three files in step.
acceptance: package.json, src-tauri/Cargo.toml and src-tauri/tauri.conf.json all read 2.3.0.

additions.title: Characterise the editor store before extending it
additions.why: The editor store is already shipped, so its current open, save, close and bin behaviour is pinned before tab repointing and close-under-folder are added.
acceptance: Existing editor store tests keep their current expectations and pass before the change.
New tests for repoint and close-under-folder fail first, then pass.
No existing expectation is weakened to make the change pass.

additions.title: Re-read open editor tabs after a file operation
additions.why: After the core renames, moves or deletes an item, the window's tab strip must show the new path or drop the closed tab.
acceptance: After a rename or move of an open file or folder, its tab stays open with the new title and path and its group is recomputed.
After a delete, the affected tabs disappear from the tab strip.
No open tab points at a path that no longer exists.

additions.title: Validate names and paths in the core before writing
additions.why: The window is not a trusted caller, so an empty, invalid or reserved name or a bad source or destination is refused before anything touches the disk.
acceptance: Empty, dot-only, separator-containing, reserved-character and reserved-device names are refused with a message.
A source that does not exist, a parent or destination that is not a folder, and a name clash are refused with a message.
A refused operation leaves the file system untouched.

additions.title: Say when Start all has no executable terminal to start
additions.why: With every terminal marked non-executable, Start all and F5 would otherwise look broken.
acceptance: Pressing Start all or F5 on an app whose terminals are all non-executable starts nothing and shows a short notice.
The notice names the cause and can be dismissed.
With at least one executable terminal the notice does not appear.

additions.title: Characterise the engine readiness loop before adding the executable filter
additions.why: The engine up action is old, shipped code; its current start-and-wait behaviour is pinned before the filter changes who it waits for.
acceptance: Existing engine up and readiness tests keep their current expectations.
A new test shows a non-executable terminal is not started and does not hold up readiness.
